rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials (oval, s-bend, slalom) of the iteration-0 design went off track with zero completions. Progress was only 0.11 to 0.16, each run had one line-loss event, and max_error (0.062 to 0.068 m) passed the 0.06 m off-track floor while rms_error stayed near 0.03 m. The robot tracks reasonably on average but loses the line and drifts out at the first sharp excursion. Steering oscillation (0.07 to 0.16) is low, so the failure is not jitter. Body width cannot raise the limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) is 0.06 for every allowed body width. The iteration-1 design was never raced, so its changes (kp 2.0, kd 0.8, speed 1.4) carry no evidence.

Changes: (1) Sensor footprint raised from 12 mm to 16 mm, so each sensor keeps reading tape as the line moves across it and the sum stays above the 0.05 line-loss threshold for longer. (2) Sensor spacing kept at 0.02 m over x = -0.04 to +0.04, with the array moved forward to y = 0.06 m so steering reacts earlier to the bend ahead. (3) base_speed reduced from 1.8 to 1.5, since a lower speed should reduce the lateral error that carries the robot off the line on the sharpest bends, while staying near the speed needed to finish in 3 s. (4) kp kept near the earlier value at 2.5 to hold a firm correction, with kd raised to 0.6 for damping. ki kept small at 0.02. (5) Mass reduced to 0.7 kg and body_length to 0.16 m, which lowers yaw inertia so the body turns more readily. Wheel track and radius are unchanged. line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events, max_error under 0.06 m on most seeds, and progress well above the previous 0.16. Completion is still uncertain because 1.5 may be slow for the 3 s limit. The main risk is that kp 2.5 is too weak on the tightest bend, so the first revision round should check the critique's claim about bend tracking.
